dedupe_keys.name: firecares community fire risk station service areas and response analytics for us fire departments

description: FireCARES (Community Assessment Response Evaluation System) is a web system that scores community fire risk and fire department performance for every registered US fire department. It is run by the International Public Safety Data Institute (IPSDI) and was built with the US Fire Administration and fire service partners to test whether station resources match a community's risk. Coverage: United States, department jurisdictions, with historical incidents from NFIRS (2024 data now loaded). Each department page combines geocoded historical fire and EMS incident heatmaps, 4, 6 and 8 minute drive-time service areas from each station, effective response force areas, structure counts by property hazard level, and live National Weather Service fire weather warnings and NIFC wildland fire perimeters. Format and access: public map pages and search by department; the underlying layers and the API need an account under a data use agreement and API terms. The FireCARES GitHub organisation publishes the processing notebooks (MIT licence) but not the data. Licence: data use agreement; free to fire departments. Caveats: NFIRS reporting is voluntary and uneven, so incident density partly reflects reporting practice; station locations are self-reported. Simulation uses: station location and service area inputs for emergency response and capacity planning models, and a validated risk layer for hazard exposure of buildings. Related records: the NFIRS public data release (data-usfa-nfirs-public-data-release) and the USFA National Fire Department Registry (data-usfa-national-fire-department-registry) are its main sources.
